clue.text: A nod or a sign and, classically, our victim appears

parts.note: a beck is a nod or gesture of summons, as in 'at one's beck and call'
and, in classical Latin, is et

explanation.surface: A gesture of assent appears, phrased in the manner of the classics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our victim' points to the puzzle's theme: Thomas Becket, the archbishop murdered in Canterbury Cathedral in 1170 after the king's outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Becket is the murdered archbishop at the centre of this themed puzzle, so he is its victim.

clue.text: Placidity, indeed — numerous Shed puzzles

parts.note: even is an intensifier like indeed, as in 'even so'

indicators.note: puzzles as a verb, meaning confuses, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A calm temperament is something many puzzles set by a setter called Shed will test.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-humouredness is a calm, equable temperament, which is placidity.

clue.text: Good egg! One lays it on the line (these do) in kind: 22 7 21 19 5 down — I wish!

indicators.note: the run of pieces is placed inside the word kind

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, the layer is placed on top of the line

parts.note: a hen lays eggs
RY is short for railway, a line
taken as written
a do or con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A rambling exclamation about a good egg laid on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the speaker of the quote spelt by 22, 7, 21, 19 and 5 down: 'Will no man rid me of this turbulent priest?', which King Henry II supposedly cried, wishing Becket gone.
explanation.definitionFit: King Henry II is reputed to have uttered the wish to be rid of Becket that led to the archbishop's murder.

clue.text: Hobbling after cross-dressing fun with tube?

indicators.note: the limping word follows the cross-dressing abbreviation

parts.note: TV is short for transvestite, a cross-dresser
game is an old word for lame, as in a game leg

explanation.surface: A limping cross-dresser has fun with a tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' means lame, as in 'a game leg'. 'Tube' is slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV game is a quiz or game show broadcast on television, the tube.

clue.text: Notes come in to my study regarding place names

indicators.note: the banknotes enter the words 'to my', sitting between them

parts.note: taken as written
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds, a sum in banknotes

explanation.surface: Musical notes interrupt someone's study of geography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks musical, but PONY is British slang for £25, a wad of banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Toponymy is the branch of onomastics concerned with the origins and meanings of geographical names.

clue.text: See 22
Change from half of nine pence for variable glasses

indicators.note: the letters are altered, swapped into a new order
only the first two of the four letters are used

parts.note: z is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Getting spectacles with the change from four and a half pence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes NI from NINE; 'Change from' rearranges NI and PENCE into PINCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pince-nez are spectacles clipped to the nose without side arms, a kind of glasses.

clue.text: See 22
Atom-splitting group 'anged the old chairman

indicators.note: breaking the atom apart rearranges its letters

parts.note: a set is a group
'anged is hanged with the H dropped, so hung becomes ung

explanation.surface: A gang of atom-splitters was hanged under the old regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting' rearranges the atom's letters. The apostrophe in 'anged marks a dropped H, Cockney style, so the past tense of hang loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mao Tse-tung, now usually spelt Mao Zedong, was Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party.

clue.text: The youngster is Peg Lear's backward daughter

parts.note: a tee is the golfer's peg on which the ball sits

indicators.note: the daughter's name is read from its end to its start

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters, as the word Lear's specifies

explanation.surface: A girl named Peg is described as King Lear's slow-witted child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a girl's name but is a golf tee; 'Lear's' tells you which daughter: Regan, from Shakespeare's King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen, a youngster.

clue.text: Hammer's cracked element with no opposition

indicators.note: the element is broken open so that the rapper's letters can sit inside it

parts.note: neon is a chemical element, the noble gas
MC Hammer is the American rapper, so Hammer gives MC

explanation.surface: A hammer has broken some chemical element without anyone objecting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' reads as a tool, but it is MC Hammer the rapper.
explanation.definitionFit: Nem con is Latin shorthand meaning unanimously, with nobody dissenting.

clue.text: See 2
Top-class drink one comes in to try — undecided

parts.note: U means upper class in British usage
a pint is a drink of beer

indicators.note: the single letter enters the word for trying

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An upper-class drinker tries again, still unable to decide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is legal: a judge hears, or tries, a case. U for upper class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in the air is an idiom for unsettled or not yet decided.

clue.text: Candid writer of love letter?

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, a zero shaped like the letter O
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: Who was the frank author of that romantic note?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love letter' is not a romantic note but the letter O, love meaning zero; the pen writes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Open and candid are synonyms for frank, honest and unconcealed.

clue.text: Goodbye to ex-PM's toothless lot!

parts.note: Anthony Eden was a British Prime Minister in the 1950s
ta-ta is an informal British farewell

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell to a former Prime Minister's ineffective team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toothless lot' sounds like a political insult, but it means the zoological order of mammals without front teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentata is an old taxonomic order of mammals such as sloths and anteaters, lacking incisors.

clue.text: See 3
Goods thus seen in airport shop at leisure?

definitions.text: Goods thus seen in airport shop
definitions.meaning: goods sold at airports without tax are labelled this way
free from work duty, off shift

explanation.definitionFit: Duty-free describes goods sold without tax, and humorously someone released from their duties.

clue.text: By the narrowest of margins, but right

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'
just means right or fair

explanation.surface: A narrow victory, though a fair one.
explanation.definitionFit: Only just is an idiom meaning barely, with almost nothing to spare.

clue.text: Eagle secured by Goosen, returning round

indicators.note: the captured letters are turned about, read from right to left
the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The golfer Retief Goosen makes an eagle on the way back in his round.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf misleads: Goosen is a golfer, eagle a score, round a game. ENRE sits inside 'goosEN REturning', and 'round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword staple.

clue.text: See 22
Sweet start to seduction: naughty try to get her arm around

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used
her and the weapon together wrap the jumbled letters

parts.note: a rifle is a firearm, an arm

explanation.surface: A seducer's opening move: a cheeky attempt to put an arm round a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' scrambles the attempt; 'get her arm around' means the woman and the weapon enclose that jumble, a picture of an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A sherry trifle is a layered British dessert of sponge, sherry, custard and cream, a sweet.

clue.text: See 22
Result of this full-blown misinterpretation — murder most foul

definitions.text: Result of this full-blown misinterpretation — murder most foul

parts.words: Result of this full-blown misinterpretation — murder most foul
parts.note: a king's angry outburst, misread by knights as an order, ended in a cathedral killing

explanation.definitionFit: Henry II's exasperated cry was taken by four knights as a command, and they killed Becket.

clue.text: God's less down

definitions.meaning: The Norse god of light, son of Odin
having less downy hair, more bald

explanation.definitionFit: Balder is a Norse deity, and as a comparative it means having less hair or fluff on the head.

clue.text: I hope it can develop a country

indicators.note: the letters are able to grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An optimistic remark that something may grow into a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a nation in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: No more fleeting Franco-German cheese celebration?

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese; the German half of the phrase applies to the celebration
Fest is the German word for a festival or party

explanation.surface: A cross-border party celebrating cheese, perhaps over too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Franco-German' splits: Franco for the French cheese, German for the German word for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nothing could be more fleeting than is the briefest, superlative of brief.

clue.text: First of slats almost off seat

indicators.note: only the first letter of the next word is taken
the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: addled describes an egg gone bad, off

explanation.surface: The front slat of a chair has nearly come off.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is the seat a rider sits on, or a bicycle seat.
